output.brief: The evidence points mainly at Callerby's own decision, not Halden. The tower crane left site in October 2025 and returned in April. The frame was stalled, and Callerby's own site notes and superintendent confirm this. The RFI platform's tamper-proof timestamps show the architect answered 62 of 64 queries on time. The 41 "late" RFIs in the draft claim mostly sat in Callerby's own draft status before submission. The structural query on CO-09 was answered in 4 days. CO-09 (MRI move, issued 6 Nov) was a real structural change. It may deserve some extension of time, but the crane had already left before it was issued. Concurrency is not yet quantified. Do not send the claim as drafted: it rests on a misleading RFI measure, and Fenmore is paid a percentage of recoveries. Commission an independent delay analysis, and use it to decide on a narrow CO-09-only claim or a settlement. Do not discipline the superintendent, who told the truth. Do not suspend the incentive scheme yet, because its link to the crane move is unproven. Review how the crane transfer was approved. Confidence is moderate to high on the RFI and crane findings, and lower on CO-09's share.
